_meta.indication: Adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC who have received prior EGFR-directed therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy (accelerated approval)

pivotal_trials.design: Global, multicenter, single-arm, open-label study of Dato-DXd monotherapy
pivotal_trials.population: TL05 enrolled 78 subjects with EGFR mutations (57% of total enrollment N=137) with advanced NSCLC previously treated with applicable targeted therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy. For FDA's efficacy evaluation, 77 patients from TL05 receiving Dato-DXd 6 mg/kg Q3W were pooled with 37 patients from TL01 (total n=114); this 114-patient EGFR-mutated pooled population is a cross-trial pooled population, not TL05's own trial population.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) by blinded independent central review (BICR) per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.n: Pooled primary efficacy population n=114 (TL05 n=77; TL01 n=37)
pivotal_trials.result: Pooled ORR by BICR 45% (95% CI: 35, 54); median DoR 6.5 months (95% CI: 4.2, 8.4)

pivotal_trials.design: Global, multicenter, randomized, active-controlled, open-label trial of Dato-DXd versus docetaxel
pivotal_trials.population: Advanced NSCLC with or without an actionable genomic alteration who received at least one prior systemic treatment; EGFR-mutated subgroup (n=37) contributed to the pooled efficacy population
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Dual primary: progression-free survival (PFS) by BICR and overall survival (OS)
pivotal_trials.n: 604 randomized (Dato-DXd 299; docetaxel 305); EGFR-mutated subgroup n=84 (Dato-DXd 39; docetaxel 45)
pivotal_trials.result: The randomized-population PFS/OS analyses in the EGFR-mutated subgroup were post-hoc and evaluated as supportive evidence only. Post-hoc EGFR-mutated subgroup: ORR by BICR 41.0% (95% CI: 25.6, 57.9) vs 8.9% (95% CI: 2.5, 21.2) with docetaxel; PFS by BICR HR 0.39 (95% CI: 0.22, 0.69), median PFS 6.8 months (95% CI: 4.2, 8.2) vs 2.7 months (95% CI: 1.5, 4.4); OS HR 0.78 (95% CI: 0.45, 1.35) crossing 1 (non-significant), median OS 15.6 months (95% CI: 12.0, 16.9) vs 12.8 months (95% CI: 6.9, 17.2)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were stomatitis (71%), nausea (50%), alopecia (49%), fatigue (42%), constipation (31%), musculoskeletal pain (22%), rash (20%), and decreased appetite (20%); serious adverse reactions in 26%; significant risks are ILD/pneumonitis, ocular toxicity, and stomatitis
target_moa: Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate; humanized IgG1 anti-Trop2 antibody linked to DXd, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a cleavable linker; upon binding Trop2 it internalizes and releases DXd causing DNA damage and apoptosis

rems.type: No safety concerns identified warranting consideration for a REMS

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR), an intermediate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in NSCLC (pooled ORR 45%)

citations.quote: ORR is a direct measure of the intervention, as in the absence of therapy, EGFR-mutated NSCLC tumors do not typically regress; for NSCLC, ORR is considered an intermediate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

confirmatory_requirement.text: TROPION-Lung15, an open-label, randomized, controlled trial of Dato-DXd with or without osimertinib versus platinum-based doublet chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated NSCLC (primary endpoint PFS by BICR; OS key secondary)

citations.quote: The trial intended to verify the clinical benefit of Dato-DXd in the treatment of patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC is TROPION-Lung15, an open-label, randomized, controlled trial comparing Dato-DXd or Dato-DXd in combination with osimertinib to platinum-doublet chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC whose disease has progressed on prior osimertinib as the most recent line of treatment.

Application Number(s)	761464
Priority or Standard	Priority

summary.text: DATROWAY received accelerated approval as a priority-review BLA for EGFR-mutated NSCLC, based on ORR as an intermediate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with continued approval contingent on the confirmatory trial TROPION-Lung15.

citations.quote: The submitted data provides substantial evidence of effectiveness to support the accelerated approval of datopotamab deruxtecan-dlnk (Dato-DXd) for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have received prior EGFR-directed therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy.
Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial, conducted as a postmarketing requirement.

requirement.text: 4860-1 Conduct a multicenter, randomized clinical trial, TROPION-LUNG15, intended to verify and describe the clinical benefit of datopotamab deruxtecan in patients with EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer who have had disease progression after osimertinib.
